name: Devin
note: The gold standard for autonomous SWE agents right now.
good: Actually completes complex multi-step coding tasks. Sandbox environment is flawless.
bad: Closed beta. Extremely expensive compute. Prone to rabbit holes if the initial prompt is vague.

name: OpenDevin
good: Fast moving. Pluggable models (works with Claude 3 Opus well).
bad: UI is still rough. Requires Docker and significant local setup. Less reliable than closed alternatives.

name: AutoGPT
note: The hype machine from 2023 that is trying to become a platform.
good: Huge community. Modular architecture in v2.
bad: Infamous for infinite loops and never actually finishing tasks. Mostly a toy for complex real-world work.

name: BabyAGI
good: The code is short enough to read and understand in an afternoon. Great learning tool.
bad: Not a production framework. Struggles with context windows on long tasks.

name: MultiOn
note: The best agent for autonomous web browsing.
good: Actually interacts with standard web UIs (clicks, types) reliably.
bad: Feels invasive as a browser extension. Can break on sites with heavy canvas/custom implementations.

name: Aider
note: My daily driver. Not 'autonomous' in the background, but the best terminal copilot.
good: Reads the whole repo via ctags. Actually commits working code. Fast.
bad: Requires you to be in the loop. Not a 'fire and forget' agent.

name: SuperAGI
note: Aiming to be the enterprise AutoGPT.
bad: Suffers from the same underlying reliability issues as all prompt-loop agents.
price: Open source free. Cloud managed available.

name: Ferris
good: Memory safe and incredibly fast execution.
bad: Ecosystem is tiny compared to Python. Very experimental.
